coverageDimensions:
SERVICE coverage: this is the only dimension the page speaks to, and it speaks to it directly. Service coverage here means "for how many AWS services can Organizations do this", and the page names them: 51 services with trusted access, 40 with delegated administrator, out of 52 rows. But the page gives only the numerator. It never states the total number of AWS services, so it cannot yield a percentage. Any ratio must be built by joining this list to an external AWS service list; on its own the page yields a positive-and-negative membership list, nothing more. Absence from the table is a real signal — a service not listed supports neither capability — but the page does not say that in words.

REGION coverage: the page gives nothing. No Region is named anywhere as a support axis. The word Region appears only inside benefit prose (managing Regions for accounts, aggregating recommendations across Regions, enabling GuardDuty in the selected Region, sharing a directory within a Region) and never as a value in a supported/not-supported statement. There is no Region column, no Region list, no "available in all Regions except" sentence. Do not synthesize Region coverage from this page.

RESOURCE TYPE coverage: the page gives nothing. No resource type is enumerated as supported or unsupported. The closest things are pointers off-page — the AWS RAM row links to a separate "Shareable Resources" page, and the AWS Agent Registry row mentions Bedrock AgentCore Runtimes and Gateways inside descriptive prose. Neither is an enumerable supported/not-supported list on this page. Resource type coverage is not even a meaningful question for these capabilities: trusted access and delegated administrator apply to accounts and services, not to resources.

features.reasoning: Trusted access is a per-service on/off fact that AWS states explicitly in its own column, and the values in that column's rows are AWS services. The universe of AWS services exists independently of AWS Organizations, so this is an external axis: a service can be absent from this table entirely, and absence means no trusted access. Caveat that must ride with any ratio: the page supplies the numerator (services that integrate) but not the denominator (all AWS services), so 51/52 is not a coverage percentage — it is 51 services with trusted access, out of a universe this page does not enumerate.
features.statuses: 51 Yes, 1 No. Read from the "Supports trusted access" column, where each cell holds an icon-yes.png or icon-no.png image followed by the literal word Yes or No. The single No is Amazon EventBridge, which is present in the table but marked No in both Yes/No columns — it is listed because the benefit prose describes cross-account event sharing, not because Organizations trusted access reaches it. Every other row is Yes.

features.featureName: Delegated administrator for AWS services (column: "Supports delegated administrator")
features.reasoning: This is a second, independent capability, not a detail of the first. The two columns disagree on 12 of 52 rows, so collapsing them into one "integrates with Organizations" fact destroys real information. Same external service axis, same denominator caveat: the page names the services that support delegated administrator, not the full set of AWS services against which that could be measured.
features.statuses: 40 Yes, 12 No. Read from the "Supports delegated administrator" column. The 12 No rows are: AWS Artifact, AWS Billing and Cost Management, AWS Control Tower, AWS Directory Service, Amazon EventBridge, Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud, AWS Marketplace, Amazon Q Developer, AWS Resource Access Manager, Service Quotas, Tag policies, AWS Well-Architected Tool. The remaining 40 rows are Yes. Note that AWS Marketplace is No while AWS Marketplace Private Marketplace and AWS Marketplace procurement insights dashboard are separate rows and both Yes.

pageTitle: AWS services that you can use with AWS Organizations
shouldNotExtract: The intro paragraphs and the two bolded definition blocks (Trusted access, Delegated administrator for AWS services) — definitions, not coverage. The "Benefits of using with AWS Organizations" column in full: it is descriptive prose and often mentions other services, Regions and resource types that are not coverage values. Every "Learn more" / "Enable trusted access" / "Enable a delegated administrator" link and its href — link targets are navigation, not data, and several rows point at the same anchor. The icon-yes.png / icon-no.png image URLs as URLs. The cross-guide links into the IAM, EC2, Config, Control Tower, Compute Optimizer, EventBridge, GuardDuty, Inspector, RAM, Route 53, Service Catalog and Billing user guides. The entire "See also" section, including the boilerplate bullet about AWS skills for AI coding assistants and the `aws agent-toolkit search-skills` command — that is appended to every AWS page and is never coverage.
trap:
Reading the table as a single list of "52 services that integrate with AWS Organizations" and reporting 52/52 supported. Two things break that. First, Amazon EventBridge is a row in the table but is marked No in BOTH columns — presence in the table is not support, and a parser that treats row existence as the Yes signal gets EventBridge wrong twice. Second, the two Yes/No columns are different capabilities that disagree on 12 rows; merging them silently converts 12 documented No answers into Yes.

Three more specific hazards. (1) The Yes/No token sits AFTER an image tag in the cell (`![](...icon-no.png) No`); a parser that strips images, or that reads the empty alt text, loses the status — the word Yes/No in the cell text is the authority, and it must agree with the icon filename. (2) Row labels are not all AWS services: "Tag policies" is an AWS Organizations policy type, and EC2 Capacity Manager, Amazon S3 Storage Lens, IAM Access Analyzer, Amazon VPC IP Address Manager, Amazon VPC Reachability Analyzer, AWS Marketplace Private Marketplace, AWS Marketplace procurement insights dashboard and AMS Self-Service Reporting are features or sub-consoles, not top-level services. Keep them as their own rows; do not normalize them up into a parent service — AWS Marketplace is No for delegated administrator while both of its sibling Marketplace rows are Yes, so collapsing them inverts the answer. (3) The Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud row's description text is wrong on the page (it describes IPAM), so never use descriptions to identify or deduplicate rows — use the row's own service name.
whatThePageStates: This page is the master compatibility matrix for AWS Organizations multi-account integration. It carries one table with 52 rows, each an AWS service (or a named service feature), and four columns: the service name plus description, the benefit of using it organization-wide, "Supports trusted access" (Yes/No), and "Supports delegated administrator" (Yes/No). The two Yes/No columns are defined in the prose above the table: trusted access lets a compatible AWS service perform operations across all accounts in the organization; delegated administrator lets a compatible AWS service register a member account as administrator for the organization in that service. The benefit column is descriptive prose and states no support fact.
